learning_policy.selection: Admit only useful source-attested English terms/phrases that enable independent explanation of an engineering/concept decision or actual runtime mechanism. Each Active item requires source paragraph, decision/concept link, precise zh-TW technical explanation, one faithful English productive sentence, and a source-bound self-comparison cue. Deduplicate by meaning and usage across articles; do not invent fillers to reach 2000.
learning_policy.sentence_requirement: At least one complete, grammatically meaningful engineering English sentence for each Active item; broader multi-context encounters may reuse it, without claiming learning outcome.
learning_policy.receptive_policy: Each prose paragraph receives a zh-TW note with canonical English terms. Active decisions remain visible passively too; tags are contextual roles, not mutually exclusive vocabulary bins.
learning_policy.four_encounters: Revisit the same original paragraphs: (1) encounter form and meaning; (2) identify decision and runtime link; (3) read or listen in context; (4) reconstruct the exact concept in English without copying, then compare to the source oracle. These are practices on the original article, never four alternate article rewrites.
learning_policy.scientific_honesty: Four-pass method is an instructional hypothesis, not a known neurological critical threshold.

reading_projection.syntax_review: Agent reviewed each complete paragraph and explicitly selected syntactic phrase/clause boundaries; word counts did not determine splits.
reading_projection.stress_scope: Cambridge-checked singular content words wall, width, queue, course, algorithm only; all other words remain plain. Identifier occurrences are excluded.
reading_projection.reason: Complete aligned English is retained in reviewed derived formatting. Pronunciation coverage is partial; no speed or comprehension outcome was observed.

decisions.title: Pair capacity and legal inputs
decisions.source_concept: A pair uses distinct ordered positions, gap width and the shorter nonnegative height.
decisions.passive: A pair uses distinct ordered positions, gap width and the shorter nonnegative height.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Explain in English how width and water height determine capacity, and why zero is a valid initial best.
decisions.oracle: The width is j - i and the water height is min(height[i], height[j]). All legal areas are nonnegative, so best may start at zero; empty and one-wall inputs are outside the contract.

decisions.title: Enumerate every legal pair before optimizing
decisions.source_concept: All-pairs visits each distinct pair once and retains only the largest evaluated area.
decisions.passive: All-pairs visits each distinct pair once and retains only the largest evaluated area.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Explain why the all-pairs enumeration covers each pair once and how its candidate count is derived.
decisions.oracle: For each i, j ranges from i + 1 through n - 1. The partner counts sum to n(n - 1)/2. Recording only their maximum is sufficient for the integer result.

decisions.title: Discard a wall only under a bound
decisions.source_concept: Keeping the shorter wall limits height while moving its partner inward reduces width.
decisions.passive: Keeping the shorter wall limits height while moving its partner inward reduces width.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Explain why the shorter wall can be discarded, including ties, and whether the next area must improve.
decisions.oracle: After evaluating the endpoints, every inward pair retaining the shorter wall is bounded by that recorded area. Equal heights allow either endpoint to be discarded. No claim says the next area is larger; moving the taller wall can miss the optimum.

decisions.title: State updates precede pointer movement
decisions.source_concept: Each iteration measures endpoints, updates best, then moves exactly one index.
decisions.passive: Each iteration measures endpoints, updates best, then moves exactly one index.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Narrate the state changes on [2, 5, 1, 4] and explain the stopping condition.
decisions.oracle: The states after moves are (1, 3, 6), (1, 2, 8) and (1, 1, 8). The last area is 1 but best stays 8. Once left equals right, no two distinct endpoints remain.

decisions.title: Python reads and bindings preserve the input
decisions.source_concept: Index reads retrieve elements; local integer rebinding does not write a list item.
decisions.passive: Index reads retrieve elements; local integer rebinding does not write a list item.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Explain which objects the implementation reads or rebinds and why height is unchanged.
decisions.oracle: Reading height[left] does not remove or copy the list. left += 1 rebinds an immutable integer local. No assignment targets a height item, and min and max only return chosen values.

decisions.title: Checkpointed coverage proves the maximum
decisions.source_concept: At each while check, evaluated and excluded pairs are covered by best.
decisions.passive: At each while check, evaluated and excluded pairs are covered by best.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: State the checkpointed invariant and connect initialization, maintenance and termination.
decisions.oracle: Before each while condition check, best is the evaluated maximum or initial zero, and every pair with an endpoint outside the interval has area at most best. The discard bound covers newly excluded pairs and best never decreases. At termination no pair remains entirely inside, and best is attained by an actual candidate unless all areas are zero.

decisions.title: Bounded work and peak live storage
decisions.source_concept: Bounded scalar operations and n - 1 iterations yield linear time and constant auxiliary space.
decisions.passive: Bounded scalar operations and n - 1 iterations yield linear time and constant auxiliary space.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Derive the time and space bounds while naming the arithmetic model and input/output conventions.
decisions.oracle: Under the bounded-integer unit-cost model, each iteration does fixed work and there are n - 1 iterations. Fixed live locals and temporaries give O(1) auxiliary and output space; the supplied O(n) input is excluded. All-pairs uses quadratic time but still fixed peak state.

decisions.title: Coordinate width preserves the discard reason
decisions.source_concept: Ordered matched coordinates replace index gaps with physical width without adding iterations.
decisions.passive: Ordered matched coordinates replace index gaps with physical width without adding iterations.
decisions.context: Read the bound original paragraphs in this article.
decisions.active_cue: Explain the width change for uneven spacing, the proof premise and the resulting costs.
decisions.oracle: Use x[right] - x[left]. Strictly increasing coordinates ensure inward movement reduces physical width, so the shorter-height bound and invariant survive. There are still n - 1 constant-work iterations and fixed live state; the supplied coordinates must already be ordered and matched to heights.
